title: What the live paper record shows
description: The engines' own state, read from the running record: what is open, what closed, and what the market filter is doing right now.
body:
Every position in this record is paper: the engines emit signals and no real orders are placed anywhere. The snapshot read at 2026-11-17T21:19:10.960Z reports what is open, what closed, and what the market filter is doing right now. It is a status report, not a projection. A single trade says nothing about a strategy, and even a short sequence of trades is only a record of what happened.

## What is open

The only open paper position named in the record is NEAR, entered at 5.896 on 12 October 2026 and open since. By contrast, each engine snapshot shows 0 open paper positions: htf-rsi-v007 shows 0, trend-daily-v005 shows 0, and trend-daily-v006 shows 0. That split is the current state, not an interpretation. The open NEAR position is a signal that has not yet closed; the engine records show no other open paper exposure at the snapshot.

The live records also have different start dates. trend-daily-v005 counts its live record from 1 October 2026, while trend-daily-v006 counts its live record from 9 October 2026. Those start dates matter for reading the closed-trade counts, because a shorter live window can contain fewer closed trades even if the underlying rule is the same. The record does not say which engine produced NEAR, so no engine is assigned to that position here.

## What has closed

The first live signal was an ATOM entry at 2.066 after the 10 October 2026 daily close. ATOM exited below its 10-day low at the 18 October 2026 close, at 1.703, which is -17.9% after the 30 bps round trip. That is a complete paper trade with a measured loss. The rule produced an entry, the market moved against the position, and the exit occurred below the 10-day low at the stated close.

The engine records add additional closed-trade aggregates. htf-rsi-v007 has 4 closed trades so far, with an average null net per trade. trend-daily-v005 has 6 closed trades so far, with an average -13.22% net per trade. trend-daily-v006 has 7 closed trades so far, with an average -13.34% net per trade. These are small counts, and the averages are negative in the trend-daily records. The htf-rsi-v007 average is recorded as null, so no average return is stated for that engine.

The testing expectation supplied with the record is that the average winner was roughly +19%, and that a losing start is the expected case rather than a surprise. Read against that expectation, the ATOM loss and the negative trend-daily averages are consistent with the stated testing pattern, but they do not prove or disprove anything. They are measurements from a short live window.

## What the market filter is allowing

Both trend-daily engines report the Bitcoin market filter as off: trend-daily-v005 is off, and trend-daily-v006 is off. At the same snapshot, both show 0 positions open on paper. The recorded state is off; the measured result is 0 open positions. No additional mechanism is stated in the record, so the report stops at that state and measurement.

The record also lists how far selected names are from their 20-day breakout. For trend-daily-v005, TRXUSDT is 13.39% below its high, ATOMUSDT is 18.95% below its high, and AAVEUSDT is 19.40% below its high. For trend-daily-v006, TRXUSDT is 13.39% below its high, JUPUSDT is 14.56% below its high, and ATOMUSDT is 18.95% below its high. These percentages are distances from the recent high, reported as the closest names to a 20-day breakout. They show how far the listed names are from that breakout level at the snapshot; they are not forecasts and do not say whether a breakout will occur.

## Where the record lives

The same numbers appear on the performance page, in the signal log, and in the status posted to the channel. The live record updates continuously, so the snapshot at 2026-11-17T21:19:10.960Z is a point-in-time reading rather than a final statement. The framing remains the same throughout: paper signals only, no real orders, and a single trade says nothing about a strategy.
